headword: {一汁三菜|いちじゅうさんさい}

definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese meal format consisting of rice, one soup, and three side dishes, considered the ideal balanced meal.

examples.japanese: ⟦{和食|わしょく}→和食：10436_washoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{基本|きほん}→基本：00226_kihon⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{一汁三菜|いちじゅうさんさい}だ。
examples.english: The basis of Japanese cuisine is one soup and three dishes.

examples.japanese: {一汁三菜|いちじゅうさんさい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{栄養|えいよう}→栄養：01882_eiyou⟧⟦バランス→バランス：03870_baransu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{整|ととの}える→整える：04259_totonoeru⟧。
examples.english: We maintain nutritional balance with a one-soup-three-dishes meal.

examples.japanese: ⟦{旅館|りょかん}→旅館：01049_ryokan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{朝食|ちょうしょく}→朝食：03122_choushoku⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{一汁三菜|いちじゅうさんさい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{定番|ていばん}→定番：12265_teiban⟧だ。
examples.english: One soup and three dishes is the standard for ryokan breakfast.

notes:
{一汁三菜|いちじゅうさんさい} represents the ideal Japanese meal structure.

ETYMOLOGY:
- ⟦{主食|しゅしょく}→主食：11408_shushoku⟧: main staple (rice)
- ⟦{汁物|しるもの}→汁物：06231_shirumono⟧: soup (usually ⟦{味噌汁|みそしる}→味噌汁：04954_misoshiru⟧)
- ⟦{主菜|しゅさい}→主菜：04995_shusai⟧: main dish (fish, meat, tofu)
- ⟦{副菜|ふくさい}→副菜：04993_fukusai⟧: two side dishes (vegetables, pickles)

FORMS:
- {一汁一菜|いちじゅういっさい}: simpler version (one soup, one dish)
- {一汁二菜|いちじゅうにさい}: one soup, two dishes

CULTURAL NOTE:
This meal format is associated with healthy eating and traditional Japanese food culture. It ensures variety and nutritional balance.
